prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a side impact at intersection claim. Injury: shoulder injury. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1015; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following a side impact collision at a controlled intersection. Insured vehicle was struck on the driver side by a vehicle that entered on a red signal. Police report requested. Claimant reports shoulder pain and has retained counsel, who has asked that all contact be routed through their office.

Entry 2: Spoke with claimant's attorney's office to confirm representation and receive the letter of representation. Requested medical authorization forms and a list of treating providers. Attorney indicated the claimant has been seen at urgent care and is scheduled for imaging of the right shoulder.

Entry 3: Reviewed photographs of both vehicles submitted by the insured. Damage consistent with a broadside impact to the driver side door and rear quarter panel. Independent appraisal assigned to the insured vehicle. Liability appears to lean toward the other driver based on the signal phase described in the statement, pending receipt of the police report and any intersection camera footage.

Entry 4: Received the medical records summary from the claimant's attorney. Records note acute right shoulder strain with limited range of motion and a follow-up orthopedic referral. No prior shoulder complaints listed in the intake history. Requested complete prior records for a five-year lookback period through counsel.

Entry 5: Left a message with the at-fault party's carrier to confirm coverage and request their recorded statement. Carrier acknowledged the claim and indicated liability is under review. File flagged for supervisor review due to represented claimant and pending orthopedic evaluation. Next diary set for follow-up with counsel once the police report is received.
